html:
The Henîa and Kamiare, known to the Spanish as the Comechingones, were Indigenous peoples of the Sierras de Córdoba and San Luis in central Argentina.

They lived in villages of partly sunken stone houses, farmed maize, beans and squash in the valleys, herded llamas and gathered carob pods. They left many rock paintings, such as those of Cerro Colorado. They were known for being tall and bearded, which surprised the Spanish. The founding of the city of Córdoba in 1573 brought Spanish rule, forced labour and epidemics, and their numbers fell sharply. Their neighbours were the Sanavirones to the north and east and the Huarpe to the west. Groups in Córdoba today claim descent from them.
sum: The Henîa and Kamiare, known to the Spanish as the Comechingones, were Indigenous peoples of the Sierras de Córdoba and San Luis in central Argentina.
